_note: The trainer scouting report's editable settings (docs/TRAINER_REPORT.md). Every threshold and list the engine uses lives here, not in code. Steps 2-4 add the matrix verdicts, bulk threshold, slider signals and tags.

lens._note: Gen IV is the primary lens: a version names its game, and that game's data (type chart, typing, stats, abilities, learnsets) is used.

level_scale._note: Every row's stats are computed at this level unless a build records its own. Change it to read teams at another level.

defaults._note: What a build gets when it leaves a field open. The report lists every default it used. Cartridge trainers keep the game's values (no EVs, their difficulty-scaled IVs).
defaults._stat_exp_note: Gen I-II have stat experience, not EVs. A Gen II build with none recorded gets the maximum in every stat (252 in EV terms), the way Showdown, Smogon's calc and the battle engine read it, so every part of the engine gives a Gen II build the same stats. The field pools follow the same default.

species_items._note: Items that work for one species line only. On anyone else they do nothing, and the check says so.

validation._note: Move legality is biological (D-048): a move counts if the species can learn it in any game of any generation, or uses it in the show, or the build records a reason. The report states the reason; only a move with no reason at all is flagged.

gen2_items._note: Gen II's own item names. PokeAPI files Gen II's berries under the Gen III names they became, so a Gen II build carrying a Gen III name is flagged with the name its game used, and a Gen III+ build carrying a Gen II-only name is flagged too. Pink Bow, Polkadot Bow and Berserk Gene exist only in Gen II.

slider_scale._note: Authored sliders run 0-100. The left pole is 0, the right pole is 100.

verdicts._note: How a type-chart multiplier becomes a word. Checked in order: the first rule that fits wins. Abilities rewrite the multiplier first.

abilities._note: Abilities that rewrite a matchup before the verdict: {ability: {attacking type: multiplier}}. 'super_effective' scales only super-effective hits; 'not_super_effective' replaces every hit that isn't. A Pokémon only gets an ability its species could have in that generation.

bulk._note: A row's bulk, from its real stats, placed in the field: physical bulk is HP x Defense, special bulk is HP x Sp. Def, each against every fully evolved Pokémon of the generation at the row's level on the default spread (0-1). A side is soft when it sits below soft_below and at least gap_at_least under the other side. HP counts: Snorlax's 65 Defense sits on 160 HP and out-bulks most of the field physically, so it isn't soft. Both sides below soft_below is frail; both at sturdy_at or more is sturdy. Only a soft side steers 'bring a physical attacker'.

team._note: The team summary, from the attacker's side. A gap is a type that hits this team hard; a strength is a type this team handles.
team._bring_note: Which attacker to bring is a team call: a side needs at least bring_at_least soft members, and bring_margin more than the other side. One soft member is named on its own, not turned into team advice.

signals._note: How the engine measures each slider from the team's data, to check the authored value. Every signal is a share of the team (0-100): how many members show it. A slider's measured value is the average of its signals that have data; a signal with no data on the team is left out, and a slider with none says 'no signal'. Weights are equal unless set. Missing data is never evidence: a member with no item recorded doesn't count for or against Choice items; a plain ball, no ribbons or no nickname say nothing about bond.

attack_heavy.label: attack-heavy stats
attack_heavy.rule: best attacking stat is higher than the average of its two defenses

damage_moves.label: mostly attacks
damage_moves.rule: at least this many of its moves deal damage

fast.label: fast
fast.rule: Speed at or above the median fully evolved Pokémon of its generation, same level and defaults

narrow_evs.label: narrow EV spreads
narrow_evs.rule: at least this share of its EVs in two stats (only builds with recorded EVs)

few_attack_types.label: low move-type variety
few_attack_types.rule: its attacks cover at most this many types

ball.label: a partner's ball (Luxury, Friend, Heal, Cherish, Premier)

risky.label: carries a gamble
risky.rule: a move under this accuracy, a one-hit KO move, recoil, a self-KO move, or one of these items

disagreement._note: When the measured value is at least this far from the authored one, the report notes it and names the signals behind it.

nature_clash._note: A nature that pulls against its trainer gets a line. Each rule: a slider and a side ('high' at or above 'at', 'low' at or below it), and the nature stats that clash. Only builds with a recorded nature are read.

rules.line: {species} has a {nature} nature: built to take hits, on a trainer who wants to deal them.
{species} has a {nature} nature: built to hit hard, on a trainer who'd rather absorb first.
{species} has a {nature} nature, trading bulk for power: a gamble on a percentage player's team.

tags._note: Report tags (not the recognition system's badges, docs/design/MASTER_PLAN.md §4.1): simple rules that fire on thresholds. A tag earns its place only if it changes a line of the report (tested).

cohesive.name: Cohesive
cohesive.rule: at least this many members share a move

type_dominant.name: Type-dominant
type_dominant.rule: at least this many members share a type

career._note: Career tags (Part 2) read each trainer's career records in canon/trainers.json, limited to the records a version has lived through. Same rule as every tag: it counts only if it changes a line (tested).

multi_region.name: Multi-Region Traveler
multi_region.rule: competed in at least this many regions

region_champion.name: {title}
region_champion.rule: a record marked champion; the tag is its title

bands._note: Where a 0-100 slider counts as low or high for the report's sentences (between is the middle).

bond_read._note: Bond is read with rigidity, never alone (it clusters high). Checked in order.

exposure._note: Your team against their attack types: a type counts when they carry a damaging move of it with at least this power (fixed-damage and variable-power moves count).

playsheet._note: The trainer playsheet (Part 2): who the ace is, who they go to in each game state, every member's roles, what they can hit, the combos to watch, signature moves, and how aggressive the moveset is. Every list and threshold here; every sentence in trainers/phrases.json (kind 'playsheet').

ace._note: The derived ace: each member scored on investment (recorded EVs, level against the team's top, friendship), support (teammates whose roles set it up), coverage (types it hits super-effectively) and role (how much its primary role wins games). An authored ace (a version's overrides.ace) is shown next to it when they differ.

supports._note: Which teammate roles set a member up. 'for' names the member's roles they help ('offense' means any offense role); 'needs' adds a condition on the member.

ace._level_note: Level counts against the team's top: the top level reads 1, ten levels below reads 0 (cartridge trainers mark their ace by level).
ace._cartridge_note: A game's own trainer sends its party out in order and marks its ace by level: when exactly one member of a cartridge team stands at the top level (Lance's Lv 50 Dragonite, Cynthia's Lv 62 Garchomp, Red's Lv 88 Pikachu), that member is the derived ace, whatever the scores say. The ranking still shows every score, and each row carries its slot (the send-out order).

go_to._note: Who they turn to in each game state: the member whose roles fit it best (role score x the state's weight for that role). Behind also lists the last resorts: members carrying a move or item that only makes sense when losing.

type_read._note: For each attacking type of the game: the hardest-hitting super-effective attack the team carries against a Pokémon of that type, at decent power (power x accuracy x STAB, with the stat it uses; a two-turn move like Dig still hits, so its turn cost doesn't count here). Coverage is how many types they reach; holes are the rest, paired with Part 1's count of how many of them are weak to each.

combos._note: Combos to watch, flagged where a team has them. scope 'member': every condition on one Pokémon; 'team': each condition met by anyone (members_at_least counts Pokémon that meet a sub-condition). Conditions: moves_any, category (a move category in trainers/roles.json), item_any, item_group, ability_any, weather (set by the team), signal_at_least (role signals).

list.name: Dragon Dance with priority or Outrage
Focus Sash with Endeavor or Reversal
A Choice lock with a way out

aggression._note: The aggression ratio: of the moves that finish (strong or priority attacks, setup, self-KOs, one-hit KOs) or wear down (status, residual damage, hazards, recovery, Protect, phazing, screens, Substitute, team healing, trapping), the share that finish. Compared with Part 1's offense slider; a gap this wide is flagged, unless Part 1 already flags the same lean.

ladder._note: The playsheet's 'On the ladder' (film/usage.py): each member's line in Smogon's newest cached monthly stats for the version's generation (Gen 4 → gen4ou, Gen 3 → gen3ou, Gen 2 → gen2ou), at the highest cutoff with at least min_raw sets behind it, and the checks that beat it most. Read from the cache only; 'film_room.py usage' fetches a month.

observations._note: Design only (Part 3 builds ingestion, and nothing lands without approval). One observation per line in canon/observations.jsonl: what a trainer did in one situation of one battle. Every fact carries where it came from and how many times it was seen.

fields.battle: a battle id (episode, cartridge fight, or your own log)
fields.situation: the game state (even, ahead, behind) and what was on the field
fields.move: what it did (a move, a switch, an item)
fields.source_ref: where exactly (episode, file and line, log)
fields.sample_size: how many times this was seen (1 for a single event; n for a tally)

provenance.lore: from the show or other canon, with a citation
provenance.derived: computed by the engine from other facts
provenance.ingested: imported from an outside source (Part 3), never trusted without a source_ref

observations.flow: propose -> approve: an ingested or derived observation is written with status 'proposed' and only counts once approved
